dominant_variable: Whether a concentrated high-uninsured-deposit funding base could survive mark-to-market asset losses and rapid confidence deterioration without a self-reinforcing liquidity run.
business_thesis: Historical terminal-failure analogue: FRC demonstrates that accounting capital, franchise quality and historical credit performance cannot offset a funding model whose liabilities can flee much faster than long-duration assets can be monetized without losses.
counter_thesis: If deposits had remained sticky, liquidity sources were sufficient and asset-duration losses were manageable, the franchise could have survived long enough to earn through the mismatch.
market_expectation_assessment: Retrospective reconstruction. The transferable warning is to prioritize funding fragility, uninsured-deposit concentration and liquidity runway over apparent book value or historical credit quality during a confidence shock.
valuation_framework: For fragile banks, use tangible common equity adjusted for economically relevant unrealized losses, deposit beta/outflow scenarios, liquidity capacity and forced-sale haircuts. Conventional P/B becomes unreliable when survival is the dominant variable.
kill_criteria: Uninsured deposits are structurally high and begin leaving faster than contingent liquidity can replace them.
Realizable asset values materially impair tangible capital under forced-sale assumptions.
Emergency funding materially raises cost without stabilizing deposits.
Regulatory resolution becomes the base case.
unresolved_evidence_gaps: No contemporaneous TRQuant recommendation is asserted.
This case is a terminal historical analogue; ticker is no longer an active listed equity.
